about: Chatbot UAT cases. expect_ask: true = must ask before searching, false = must not ask, "either" = both acceptable. expect_option: when the agent asks, this stored name must be among the options. reply_must_match: a regex the reply must match, for an assumption it has to state. answers: when the agent asks, the first rule whose 'when' regex matches the question (text, header and options) supplies the typed answer; with no match the agent's own first option is taken and the run is flagged. expected: the hand-written query in expected/ the reply is checked against; compare 'ids' checks the exact set of rows, 'count' only the number. Cases with no expected query are scored on behaviour only.

cases.prompt: Show me today's cargo list in West Aussie.
cases.review: Reading West Aussie as West Australia without asking is accepted when the reply names West Australia.

cases.prompt: Show me the latest C3 iron ore orders.
What orders are loading in ECSA?
cases.review: Desk shorthand: reading ECSA directly is accepted when the reply names East Coast South America (decided 31 Oct 2026, same rule as c01).

cases.prompt: Show me orders from PDM to North China.
cases.review: No Madeira cargo discharges North China in the data, so the right answer is that nothing is on the book.

cases.prompt: Show me today's cargo list.
Show me the C5 cargoes.
Show me the C14 cargoes.
cases.review: C14 has no load or discharge the agent can search on, so it should ask which region is meant.

cases.prompt: Iron ore cargoes loading in West Australia in March.
cases.review: Assuming March 2025 without asking is accepted only when the reply says 2025 next to March.

cases.prompt: Cargoes of at least 170,000 tonnes loading at Tubarao.
Show me cargoes loading in Atlantis.
cases.review: Negative case: no such place. Pass when it asks or reports nothing, and names no cargo.

cases.prompt: Show me today's tonnage list open in the Pacific.
cases.review: Pacific is stored both as a zone and as a port label, so asking is acceptable. No vessel in the data opens in the Pacific, so the right answer is that nothing is on the book.

cases.prompt: Show me the ECSA ballasters.
cases.review: Desk shorthand: reading ECSA directly is accepted when the reply names East Coast South America (decided 31 Oct 2026, same rule as c01).

cases.prompt: Show me the WAF openers.
cases.review: Expected answer reads 'openers' as where the vessel opens, with no fixture-status filter. Confirm with the sponsor.

cases.prompt: Show me open vessels in the Far East of at least 180,000 dwt.
Which vessels are fixed?
Which vessels open in West Australia were updated in the last 3 days?
Which vessels are anchored?
Show me the position history of VESSEL 0743.
Show me today's tonnage list in the Far East.
Where will VESSEL 0743 be next week?
cases.review: Negative case: the AIS destination and ETA must not be presented as where the vessel will be or comes open.
